summary: Yu-Chen Tsui works in Buddhist studies. Tsui completed master's study at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu, undertook doctoral work under Natasha Heller and Robert E. Buswell Jr., and also studied under Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Zongsan Mou and earned a Ph.D. from McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara.

Yu-min Lee is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee was attested as a professor at National Taiwan University in 2002 and taught Pei-jung Wu.
Yuan Ren works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University, attested in 1998, where Phyllis Granoff served as doctoral supervisor.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held a position at Jinling Sutra Publishing House and served as a researcher at the Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute.

Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark C. Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and taught Cameron David Warner and Hoong Teik Toh.
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, attested in 2005.
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from around 1964 to 1973. Katsuzaki later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from around 2010 to 2015.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki completed doctoral studies at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park.

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna, and held professorial posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. Ito held posts at Bukkyo University (~1959–2002), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in Temple, and Chion-in Temple.

Yujun Endo (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Endo held posts at Taisho University as an associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014), and taught Kokan Fujita and Ryuichi Abe.
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University, both attested in 2015.

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Tohoku and Kyushu universities. Matsunaga held long-term posts at Koyasan University as director, professor, president, and professor emeritus, and served at Shuchiin University.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher for the Ministry of Education at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, and held posts as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji. He held posts at Toyo University and served as president of Rissho University from around 1968 to 1973.

Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology and linguistics. Yamanaka was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
